cards.text: God is still giving Moses words to pass on to the Israelites. He's covered servants, oxen, lawsuits and feasts. Now He looks down the road ahead, and He's sending someone out in front of them.

cards.question: Who does God say He's sending ahead of the Israelites?
What does God say the angel will do for the Israelites along the way?

answers.text: Protect them and bring them to the place God prepared
Teach them the laws and settle every one of their disputes
Count the tribes and choose the leaders for each one

cards.text: Then God gives a heads-up about this angel: pay attention to him, listen to his voice, and do not defy him. Friend, this is NOT a GPS you tune out because you "know a shortcut."

cards.question: God says the Israelites must not defy the angel. What reason does He give?

answers.text: He will turn back to Egypt
He will go to another people

cards.question: God says His Name is in the angel He's sending ahead of Israel.

cards.text: Now the flip side. If they listen carefully to the angel's voice and do everything God says, God makes them a promise.

cards.question: If the Israelites listen and obey, what does God promise to do about their enemies?

answers.text: Be an enemy to their enemies

cards.text: That's not a pinky promise, friend. Israel's enemies just became GOD'S enemies. Then He names the land His angel is leading them into: the land of the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites and Jebusites.

cards.question: Six nations live in that land. What does God say He'll do to them?

cards.text: Those nations come with their own gods. And God doesn't leave Israel guessing about what to do with them.

cards.question: God says Israel can follow the nations' practices, as long as they don't bow down to their gods.
Instead, God tells Israel to demolish the nations' gods and smash their sacred ___ to pieces.

cards.text: Instead of all that, they're to serve the LORD their God. And His blessing doesn't wait around for the big moments.

cards.question: When they serve Him, God says He will bless their ___ and their ___.
Along with blessing the everyday basics, God promises to take away sickness from among them.

cards.text: God keeps going. No woman in their land will miscarry or be barren, and He says, 'I will fulfill the number of your days.' Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer counting falling dust, so days God fills up? That's a count I'll take ANY day.

God is still telling Moses what's ahead for the Israelites as they head into the land. Before they even arrive, He's sending His terror ahead of them. He'll throw into confusion every nation they meet.

cards.question: When God's terror reaches Israel's enemies, what does God say they'll do?

cards.text: That's not the only thing God sends on ahead. The next one is a whole lot smaller.

cards.question: What does God send before Israel to drive the Hivites, Canaanites and Hittites out of the way?

cards.text: The HORNET! One hornet buzzes into my bakery and I'm diving behind the oven, gold base and all. But here's the twist: God says He won't drive the nations out in a single year.

cards.question: God won't drive the nations out of the land in a single year. Why not?

answers.text: The land would become desolate and wild animals would multiply
Israel would not be ready to fight every battle in one year
The nations would band together and attack Israel all at once

cards.question: So God will drive them out little by little, until Israel becomes ___ and possesses the land.

cards.text: Then God sketches the borders: from the Red Sea to the Sea of the Philistines, and from the desert to the Euphrates. Friend, my whole territory used to be the back of a takeout menu in a junk drawer.

cards.question: God says He will deliver the land's inhabitants into Israel's hand, and Israel will drive them out.

cards.text: Now God gets to one last warning. It's about how Israel deals with these nations and their gods.

cards.question: Israel may make a covenant with these nations, as long as it doesn't include their gods.
God says these nations must not remain in Israel's land. What reason does He give?

answers.text: They would cause Israel to sin against Him
They would take the best fields for themselves
They would grow and outnumber the Israelites

cards.text: And God ends with this: 'For if you serve their gods, it will surely be a snare to you.' A snare is the trap you don't see until you're stuck, like opening one group chat "real quick" and looking up an hour later.

findings.problem: The opening card states facts from outside the passage (God has already covered servants, oxen, lawsuits and feasts, from Exodus 21-23) but cites only Exodus 23:20. Those outside facts carry no reference.

rule.text: Facts from outside the passage are fine when they help, like who a new person is or who wrote a letter, with their reference.

findings.problem: "Israel's enemies just became GOD'S enemies" is stated as a Bible fact, not a joke. It drops the condition in Exodus 23:22 ("if you will listen carefully... and do everything I say"). It also turns a future promise ("I will be an enemy") into something that has already happened ("just became").

rule.text: Don't stretch the text. Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: The blank in "smash their sacred ___ to pieces" (stones, scrolls or robes) asks the baker to guess an unseen detail word. Nothing on the earlier cards lets them reason it out. This is the same as the Psalm 23 bad example of guessing what David's head is anointed with.

rule.text: The rule against guessing the next words of a line (see below) applies to every passage, and to fill in the blank too. The blank tests meaning the baker can reason out, not wording they haven't seen.

findings.problem: "Bless their ___ and their ___" (bread, water, tents, cattle, gold) asks the baker to guess the exact words of the line. The setup on card 14 ("doesn't wait around for the big moments") fits tents and cattle as well as bread and water, so the pick comes down to luck.

rule.text: The check: could a thoughtful baker who has only seen the earlier cards make a reasoned pick? If the only way to get it right is luck, give the story card more context or ask a different question.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences. Its joke is also hard to follow ("so days God fills up? That's a count I'll take ANY day"). Split the card or trim it.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences. Only the opening card of the walkthrough may have up to 3 sentences. Its first sentence ("God is still telling Moses what's ahead...") also reads like a recap rather than moving the passage forward.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: This story card has three sentences: the hornet exclamation, the bakery joke, and the setup for card 6.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: Nothing on the earlier cards hints at the reason God gives for not driving the nations out in one year. Both wrong answers (Israel not ready to fight, the nations banding together) are just as reasonable, so this is a pure discovery pick. Card 5 could give more context, for example by pointing to the land itself.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: The card spends its first half defining the hard word "snare" ("A snare is the trap you don't see until you're stuck"). The dictionary pop-up already covers it. The group chat comparison can carry the moment without the definition.

rule.text: Don't spend card words explaining a hard word. Hard words get a dictionary pop-up (definitions.md, made after the cards).
